findings.body: The UI reports two pages instead of one, enables Next, and allows navigation to an empty phantom page.
findings.failure_mode: Pagination overcounts whenever there is no remainder.
findings.impact: The UI reports two pages instead of one, enables Next, and allows navigation to an empty phantom page.
findings.root_cause: The page-count calculation floors the quotient and then unconditionally adds one.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the page count with `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` while retaining the explicit zero-member case.
findings.title: Exact page-size multiples produce a phantom extra page
findings.trigger: Open an admin group whose member count is an exact positive multiple of the page limit, such as 50 members with a limit of 50.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 13 shows `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` which always adds 1 after flooring. For 50 users with limit 50, this yields floor(50/50)+1=2 pages instead of 1. The trigger and impact are realistic.

raw_findings.body: Only the first 50 members are displayed because the public route uses the default limit and the public template has no controls for requesting subsequent pages.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Public member listings silently omit all members after the first page.
raw_findings.impact: Only the first 50 members are displayed because the public route uses the default limit and the public template has no controls for requesting subsequent pages.
raw_findings.root_cause: A default limit was applied to every group-members request while pagination was added only to the admin interface.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add pagination state and controls to the public group-members page, or preserve the previous unbounded behavior for that UI until pagination is implemented.
raw_findings.title: The public member list is truncated without pagination controls
raw_findings.trigger: Visit the public members page for a visible group containing more than 50 users.

raw_findings.body: The client receives an object containing `members` and `meta` instead of an array, causing array iteration and deserialization code to fail.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing consumers cannot deserialize the response they previously supported.
raw_findings.impact: The client receives an object containing `members` and `meta` instead of an array, causing array iteration and deserialization code to fail.
raw_findings.root_cause: Pagination metadata was introduced by replacing, rather than compatibly extending or versioning, the endpoint's response shape.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the array response and expose pagination metadata through headers, or introduce/version a new endpoint and retain the old contract during a deprecation period.
raw_findings.title: The members endpoint breaks its existing JSON response contract
raw_findings.trigger: An existing API client or plugin calls `/groups/:group_id/members.json` and parses the response as the previously returned array.

raw_findings.body: The reload still requests offset 50 using the stale pre-deletion count; the server then reports a total of 50 with no members, leaving the UI on an empty page until the admin manually goes back.
raw_findings.evidence: var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));
raw_findings.failure_mode: Membership changes can strand pagination beyond the final valid record.
raw_findings.impact: The reload still requests offset 50 using the stale pre-deletion count; the server then reports a total of 50 with no members, leaving the UI on an empty page until the admin manually goes back.
raw_findings.root_cause: The reload clamps the offset against the model's stale member count rather than the post-mutation total.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After receiving the new total, detect an offset at or beyond the total, move to the last valid page offset, and refetch; alternatively update and clamp the count/offset before the post-removal reload.
raw_findings.title: Deleting the sole member on the last page leaves an empty out-of-range page
raw_findings.trigger: A group has 51 members with a page size of 50, and an admin removes the sole member while viewing the second page.

raw_findings.body: A response for an older offset can apply after the response for the latest click, sending the displayed member list and page indicator backward to the stale page.
raw_findings.evidence:
self.setProperties({
        user_count: result.meta.total,
        limit: result.meta.limit,
        offset: result.meta.offset,
        members: result.members.map(function(member) { return Discourse.User.create(member); })
raw_findings.failure_mode: Network response order, rather than the user's last action, determines the displayed page.
raw_findings.impact: A response for an older offset can apply after the response for the latest click, sending the displayed member list and page indicator backward to the stale page.
raw_findings.root_cause: Every asynchronous response unconditionally replaces shared pagination state without checking whether it corresponds to the latest request.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Disable pagination while a request is pending, serialize navigation requests, or attach a request token and ignore responses that are no longer current.
raw_findings.title: Concurrent page requests can overwrite the newest selection
raw_findings.trigger: An admin clicks Next more than once before the first members request completes, and the responses arrive out of order.

raw_findings.body: Because the form has no submit action or prevented default, the browser submits to the current URL and can reload/navigate away, losing unsaved edits.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Keyboard form submission bypasses the application's save workflow.
raw_findings.impact: Because the form has no submit action or prevented default, the browser submits to the current URL and can reload/navigate away, losing unsaved edits.
raw_findings.root_cause: Existing controls were wrapped in a native form without adding submit handling.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Bind the form's submit event to the `save` action while preventing the native submission, and mark non-submit action buttons with `type="button"`.
raw_findings.title: The new form performs an unhandled browser submission on Enter
raw_findings.trigger: An admin presses Enter while editing the group name or another field instead of clicking the Ember action button.

raw_findings.body: The endpoint attempts to create the same `GroupUser` association again instead of treating the operation as a no-op, which can fail with an association uniqueness error and prevent the batch from completing normally.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A valid repeat request is not idempotent and can terminate with a server error.
raw_findings.impact: The endpoint attempts to create the same `GroupUser` association again instead of treating the operation as a no-op, which can fail with an association uniqueness error and prevent the batch from completing normally.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new add-members loop does not check current membership before calling the association insertion helper.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Skip users already present in the group or use an idempotent `find_or_create` operation, ideally inside a transaction for the whole batch.
raw_findings.title: Adding an existing member attempts a duplicate association write
raw_findings.trigger: An admin enters a username that already belongs to the group, or repeats an add request after a timeout or double-click.

raw_findings.body: The negative value is passed to ActiveRecord's SQL `OFFSET` or `LIMIT`, causing PostgreSQL to reject the query and the endpoint to return a server error instead of a bounded client response.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Malformed pagination input reaches the database as invalid SQL pagination state.
raw_findings.impact: The negative value is passed to ActiveRecord's SQL `OFFSET` or `LIMIT`, causing PostgreSQL to reject the query and the endpoint to return a server error instead of a bounded client response.
raw_findings.root_cause: Untrusted pagination parameters are converted to integers but never range-validated.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp offset to zero or greater and constrain limit to a positive server-defined maximum before constructing the query.
raw_findings.title: Negative pagination parameters can turn a public request into a database error
raw_findings.trigger: A client requests a group-members URL with a negative `offset` or `limit`, such as `?offset=-1`.

raw_findings.body: The request now enters the generic update action, ignores the membership changes, and can additionally set `visible` to false because that parameter is absent, despite returning a successful response.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing incremental membership requests silently mutate the wrong state and do not perform the requested operation.
raw_findings.impact: The request now enters the generic update action, ignores the membership changes, and can additionally set `visible` to false because that parameter is absent, despite returning a successful response.
raw_findings.root_cause: The method-specific PATCH branch was deleted without preserving or versioning the existing endpoint behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Retain the PATCH membership handler as a compatibility path while introducing the new member endpoints, then deprecate it explicitly before removal.
raw_findings.title: Removing PATCH dispatch silently breaks incremental membership updates
raw_findings.trigger: An existing client sends the established `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` request with `changes[add]` or `changes[delete]`.

raw_findings.body: The controller reads an empty top-level name and returns a validation error, so clients using the previous request format can no longer create groups.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Previously valid create requests are rejected.

raw_findings.root_cause: The create action switched from nested group parameters to top-level parameters without compatibility handling or endpoint versioning.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Read attributes from `params[:group]` when present, with the new flat parameters as a fallback, and preserve legacy initial-membership behavior during a deprecation period.
raw_findings.title: Existing nested create payloads no longer create groups
raw_findings.trigger: An existing client sends the former create contract, `{ group: { name: "team", visible: "true", usernames: "alice" } }`.

raw_findings.failure_mode: Legacy updates report success while applying unintended state and discarding requested changes.

validated_findings.body: The UI reports two pages instead of one, enables Next, and allows navigation to an empty phantom page.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Pagination overcounts whenever there is no remainder.
validated_findings.impact: The UI reports two pages instead of one, enables Next, and allows navigation to an empty phantom page.
validated_findings.root_cause: The page-count calculation floors the quotient and then unconditionally adds one.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the page count with `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` while retaining the explicit zero-member case.
validated_findings.title: Exact page-size multiples produce a phantom extra page
validated_findings.trigger: Open an admin group whose member count is an exact positive multiple of the page limit, such as 50 members with a limit of 50.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 13 shows `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` which always adds 1 after flooring. For 50 users with limit 50, this yields floor(50/50)+1=2 pages instead of 1. The trigger and impact are realistic.

validated_findings.body: Only the first 50 members are displayed because the public route uses the default limit and the public template has no controls for requesting subsequent pages.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Public member listings silently omit all members after the first page.
validated_findings.impact: Only the first 50 members are displayed because the public route uses the default limit and the public template has no controls for requesting subsequent pages.
validated_findings.root_cause: A default limit was applied to every group-members request while pagination was added only to the admin interface.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add pagination state and controls to the public group-members page, or preserve the previous unbounded behavior for that UI until pagination is implemented.
validated_findings.title: The public member list is truncated without pagination controls
validated_findings.trigger: Visit the public members page for a visible group containing more than 50 users.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 22 shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` applying pagination to all groups. The public template at group/members.hbs shows no pagination controls, only iterating members. Groups with >50 members would be truncated without navigation.

validated_findings.body: The client receives an object containing `members` and `meta` instead of an array, causing array iteration and deserialization code to fail.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Existing consumers cannot deserialize the response they previously supported.
validated_findings.impact: The client receives an object containing `members` and `meta` instead of an array, causing array iteration and deserialization code to fail.
validated_findings.root_cause: Pagination metadata was introduced by replacing, rather than compatibly extending or versioning, the endpoint's response shape.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the array response and expose pagination metadata through headers, or introduce/version a new endpoint and retain the old contract during a deprecation period.
validated_findings.title: The members endpoint breaks its existing JSON response contract
validated_findings.trigger: An existing API client or plugin calls `/groups/:group_id/members.json` and parses the response as the previously returned array.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 28-35 show the new response shape is an object with `members` and `meta` keys. Previously (LEFT side L32) it was `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` returning an array. This is a breaking API change for existing consumers.

validated_findings.body: The reload still requests offset 50 using the stale pre-deletion count; the server then reports a total of 50 with no members, leaving the UI on an empty page until the admin manually goes back.
validated_findings.evidence: var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));
validated_findings.failure_mode: Membership changes can strand pagination beyond the final valid record.
validated_findings.impact: The reload still requests offset 50 using the stale pre-deletion count; the server then reports a total of 50 with no members, leaving the UI on an empty page until the admin manually goes back.
validated_findings.root_cause: The reload clamps the offset against the model's stale member count rather than the post-mutation total.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: After receiving the new total, detect an offset at or beyond the total, move to the last valid page offset, and refetch; alternatively update and clamp the count/offset before the post-removal reload.
validated_findings.title: Deleting the sole member on the last page leaves an empty out-of-range page
validated_findings.trigger: A group has 51 members with a page size of 50, and an admin removes the sole member while viewing the second page.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 23 shows `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)` clamping against stale user_count before the request. After deletion, the server returns new total but offset was already sent. The UI could show empty page until manual navigation.

validated_findings.body: A response for an older offset can apply after the response for the latest click, sending the displayed member list and page indicator backward to the stale page.
validated_findings.evidence:
self.setProperties({
        user_count: result.meta.total,
        limit: result.meta.limit,
        offset: result.meta.offset,
        members: result.members.map(function(member) { return Discourse.User.create(member); })
validated_findings.failure_mode: Network response order, rather than the user's last action, determines the displayed page.
validated_findings.impact: A response for an older offset can apply after the response for the latest click, sending the displayed member list and page indicator backward to the stale page.
validated_findings.root_cause: Every asynchronous response unconditionally replaces shared pagination state without checking whether it corresponds to the latest request.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Disable pagination while a request is pending, serialize navigation requests, or attach a request token and ignore responses that are no longer current.
validated_findings.title: Concurrent page requests can overwrite the newest selection
validated_findings.trigger: An admin clicks Next more than once before the first members request completes, and the responses arrive out of order.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 31-35 show `self.setProperties` unconditionally applying response data without checking if it corresponds to the latest request. Rapid pagination clicks with out-of-order responses could display stale data.

validated_findings.body: Because the form has no submit action or prevented default, the browser submits to the current URL and can reload/navigate away, losing unsaved edits.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Keyboard form submission bypasses the application's save workflow.
validated_findings.impact: Because the form has no submit action or prevented default, the browser submits to the current URL and can reload/navigate away, losing unsaved edits.
validated_findings.root_cause: Existing controls were wrapped in a native form without adding submit handling.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Bind the form's submit event to the `save` action while preventing the native submission, and mark non-submit action buttons with `type="button"`.
validated_findings.title: The new form performs an unhandled browser submission on Enter
validated_findings.trigger: An admin presses Enter while editing the group name or another field instead of clicking the Ember action button.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1 shows `<form class="form-horizontal">` without any submit handler or action attribute. Pressing Enter in text fields would trigger native form submission, potentially navigating away and losing edits.

validated_findings.body: The endpoint attempts to create the same `GroupUser` association again instead of treating the operation as a no-op, which can fail with an association uniqueness error and prevent the batch from completing normally.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A valid repeat request is not idempotent and can terminate with a server error.
validated_findings.impact: The endpoint attempts to create the same `GroupUser` association again instead of treating the operation as a no-op, which can fail with an association uniqueness error and prevent the batch from completing normally.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new add-members loop does not check current membership before calling the association insertion helper.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Skip users already present in the group or use an idempotent `find_or_create` operation, ideally inside a transaction for the whole batch.
validated_findings.title: Adding an existing member attempts a duplicate association write
validated_findings.trigger: An admin enters a username that already belongs to the group, or repeats an add request after a timeout or double-click.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The `group.add(user)` method at app/models/group.rb:272-273 uses `self.users.push(user)` which is idempotent in Rails - adding an existing association member is a no-op. No duplicate association error would occur.

validated_findings.body: The negative value is passed to ActiveRecord's SQL `OFFSET` or `LIMIT`, causing PostgreSQL to reject the query and the endpoint to return a server error instead of a bounded client response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Malformed pagination input reaches the database as invalid SQL pagination state.
validated_findings.impact: The negative value is passed to ActiveRecord's SQL `OFFSET` or `LIMIT`, causing PostgreSQL to reject the query and the endpoint to return a server error instead of a bounded client response.
validated_findings.root_cause: Untrusted pagination parameters are converted to integers but never range-validated.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Clamp offset to zero or greater and constrain limit to a positive server-defined maximum before constructing the query.
validated_findings.title: Negative pagination parameters can turn a public request into a database error
validated_findings.trigger: A client requests a group-members URL with a negative `offset` or `limit`, such as `?offset=-1`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 22-23 show `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no validation. Negative values would be passed to SQL OFFSET/LIMIT, causing PostgreSQL errors.

validated_findings.body: The request now enters the generic update action, ignores the membership changes, and can additionally set `visible` to false because that parameter is absent, despite returning a successful response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Existing incremental membership requests silently mutate the wrong state and do not perform the requested operation.
validated_findings.impact: The request now enters the generic update action, ignores the membership changes, and can additionally set `visible` to false because that parameter is absent, despite returning a successful response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The method-specific PATCH branch was deleted without preserving or versioning the existing endpoint behavior.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Retain the PATCH membership handler as a compatibility path while introducing the new member endpoints, then deprecate it explicitly before removal.
validated_findings.title: Removing PATCH dispatch silently breaks incremental membership updates
validated_findings.trigger: An existing client sends the established `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` request with `changes[add]` or `changes[delete]`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The finding cites LEFT side line 65 showing PATCH dispatch was removed. However, this is about backward compatibility with old API contracts, not a bug introduced by the patch. The patch intentionally changed the API design.

validated_findings.body: The controller reads an empty top-level name and returns a validation error, so clients using the previous request format can no longer create groups.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Previously valid create requests are rejected.
validated_findings.impact: The controller reads an empty top-level name and returns a validation error, so clients using the previous request format can no longer create groups.
validated_findings.root_cause: The create action switched from nested group parameters to top-level parameters without compatibility handling or endpoint versioning.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Read attributes from `params[:group]` when present, with the new flat parameters as a fallback, and preserve legacy initial-membership behavior during a deprecation period.
validated_findings.title: Existing nested create payloads no longer create groups
validated_findings.trigger: An existing client sends the former create contract, `{ group: { name: "team", visible: "true", usernames: "alice" } }`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 24 shows `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip` reading from top-level params. Old clients sending `{group: {name: ...}}` would get empty name. This breaks backward compatibility.

validated_findings.body: The requested name and alias changes are ignored, while the absent top-level `visible` parameter is interpreted as false, so the request can return success after unexpectedly hiding the group.

group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?

    # group rename is ignored for automatic groups

validated_findings.failure_mode: Legacy updates report success while applying unintended state and discarding requested changes.
validated_findings.impact: The requested name and alias changes are ignored, while the absent top-level `visible` parameter is interpreted as false, so the request can return success after unexpectedly hiding the group.
validated_findings.root_cause: The update action flattened its parameter contract and treats a missing top-level visibility field as an explicit false value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize `payload = params[:group] || params` and read all update attributes from that payload, or version the breaking request contract.

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 115 shows `xhr :put, :remove_member` but config/routes.rb:49 shows `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. The test uses PUT while production route is DELETE, so test doesn't exercise actual endpoint.
